title: Pre-dawn orders and a rainy truck ride on Leyte
summary: Woken at three after little sleep, the show flew to the island of Lahti in downpours and rode standing in an open truck.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: like a ton of bricks. Now, you've gone to bed and your head is like that. I had slept about two hours, and here comes Sylvester waking everybody up: "Pack up." So we packed up. We had to meet the plane at about six o'clock. Oh, brother, my head was bustin' open, and I know some of the rest of them felt worse than I did.

So we go and meet the plane at six o'clock in the morning, boy. We had about two hours sleep. So we get in the plane, and we're on our way to Lahti(?), goin' to Lahti(?). And we get into Lahti, and it's rainin' cats and dogs. It is raining. It's pouring. And the plane stops in the middle of a big field. There's nothing in sight. Ain't even a tree in sight. Nothing! The plane comes down. He says, "All right." So Sylvester says, "Is there something here to move us or something?" And he said, "Well, the truck will be around to pick you up."

Okay, we get out of the plane, we get in this field, and there we are, standing up in the field early in the morning, and it's pouring brickbats out there. Oh, that rain is comin' down. So there we stand out there. And everybody, they don't feel good anyway. Pretty soon, here comes the truck. And I forget what the truck is called. It's not a weapons carrier. That's big enough to stand up in if they got a cover on it, you know. But this one you

could stand up in, but it didn't have no cover on it. There was supposed to be a cover on it, but there was no cover. Now, we got to stand up in this truck and go to our area, our camp where we're designated. And it was quite a ride. Quite a ride. And we had to stand up all the way in the rain, the rain beatin' you in the face if you're looking where you're going. And if you turn the other way, it's beatin' you all in the rear parts of you. But anyway, it's still raining; it's pouring there.

So anyway, we get to the staging area, our little camp. We get in the tents, we divide up the tents between us. Thirteen in the show, divide it up by thirteen people. The women, they've got their own little tents, and the men had the rest. Well, we get all settled there, and then in walks the Special Service Officer. That was in the afternoon when he gets there. So he is... Well, see, we had been so accustomed to not doing anything in Manila for the past month... For most of the month we didn't do a thing! So bad as we felt from the night before, we knew we wasn't gonna do anything that night, too. We knew we were going to work, because it was raining too hard. Oh, it was throwing brickbats!
